title: Telemetry catalog service
summary: A standalone, database-free HTTP System Under Test for constraint and validation work: a telemetry catalog whose documented rules decide whether a submitted record is accepted.

lifecycle.install: none — Python standard library only, no database
lifecycle.health: python <sut>/selftest.py — boots the service and exercises every validation rule over HTTP
lifecycle.stop: terminate the service process; it holds no external state

determinism.reset: In-memory only: restarting the process returns it to the documented baseline catalog.
determinism.seed: No seed needed: validation is a pure function of the submitted record and the declared rules.

oracle.description: The declared telemetry rules decide acceptance; the scenario TAIL parses the HTTP response and maps rule outcomes onto Bundle verdict codes.
oracle.independence: The rule set is declared separately from the service's request handler and is re-stated in the scenario's constraint sidecar, so a rule the service applies but the scenario does not expect surfaces as a disagreement rather than being absorbed.

known_pass: telemetry_catalog_e2e: a record satisfying every declared rule is accepted
known_fail: telemetry_catalog_e2e: records violating each individual rule are rejected with that rule's reason

cleanup: Stop the service process; python generator_trunk/bundle_run.py cleanup <run-dir>.
caveats: Candidates reach a loopback HTTP target, so the intended row uses networked-api-probe — never trusted-local.

The current tests prove the independent oracle, live HTTP behaviour, and direct full pipeline, but do not yet prove that exact networked-api-probe container-policy row end to end. It is reference, not canonical, until that gate exists.
